title: Ferrand scheme pushouts are pushouts of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:Z\to T$ be morphisms of $S$-schemes, with $i$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] and $j$ integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Suppose that for every $t\in T$ there is an affine open $U\subseteq X$ containing $i(j^{-1}(\{t\}))$. Let $P$, with maps $a:X\to P$ and $b:T\to P$, be a pushout of this diagram in schemes [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Regard these schemes as algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Then the same cocone is a pushout in algebraic spaces over $S$: for every algebraic space $H/S$, every pair $f:X\to H$, $g:T\to H$ with $fi=gj$ admits a unique $h:P\to H$ satisfying $ha=f$ and $hb=g$.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-ferrand-scheme-pushout] with exactly the stated closed-immersion, integrality and fibre-neighbourhood hypotheses. Its scheme pushout is uniquely isomorphic to the given $P$, compatibly with $a,b,i,j$, by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: the maps supplied in both directions compose to the identity because they agree on both legs. This also identifies their structure maps to $S$. Thus the quotient-space description in that node makes $a$ and $b$ jointly surjective. The given scheme pushout is also a pushout among $S$-schemes: for compatible $S$-maps into an $S$-scheme $H$, the scheme extension is over $S$, since its composite to $S$ and the structure map of $P$ agree after $a$ and $b$ and hence are equal by uniqueness.

Let $q:U\to P$ be any etale morphism from a scheme. The converse assertion of [lem-sfb-ferrand-etale-scheme-patching] says that $U$ is the scheme pushout of $U\times_PX$ and $U\times_PT$ along $U\times_PZ$. Its assertion explicitly allows nonseparated and non-quasi-compact $q$. The same uniqueness argument as in step 1, now applied to maps to $S$, makes this a pushout of $S$-schemes. Thus every etale base change satisfies hypothesis (ii) of [lem-sfb-scheme-colimit-upgrade-space-targets].

Take a compatible family of etale schemes over the three vertices of the span $X\leftarrow Z\to T$, with separated structure maps. Its cartesian transition squares identify its $Z$-component with both $X'\times_XZ$ and $T'\times_TZ$, giving their specified isomorphism $\phi$. Apply the forward assertion of [lem-sfb-ferrand-etale-scheme-patching]. It supplies the scheme $P'$ etale over $P$ and canonical isomorphisms of its three pullbacks with these components, respecting $\phi$ and the projections. Therefore it supplies an isomorphism of the entire compatible family with the pullback family; this is precisely the essential-image condition (iii) of the colimit criterion.

Apply [lem-sfb-scheme-colimit-upgrade-space-targets] with base $S$ and the finite span category having objects $Z,X,T$ and two nonidentity arrows $Z\to X,Z\to T$. This category is small in the fixed universe; step 1 gives its scheme colimit and joint surjectivity, step 2 gives the colimits after every etale scheme base change, and step 3 gives descent of every separated etale compatible family. The conclusion of that node identifies maps $P\to H$ bijectively with compatible families into any algebraic space $H/S$. For a span such a family is exactly a pair $f:X\to H$, $g:T\to H$ with $fi=gj$ (the $Z$-map is their common composite), so the bijection gives the required existence and uniqueness of $h$.

lean.statement: theorem ferrand_pushout_space_agreement (S : Scheme.{u}) (Z X T P : Over S) (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : Z ⟶ T) (a : X ⟶ P) (b : T ⟶ P) [IsClosedImmersion i.left] [IsIntegralHom j.left] (hAffine : ∀ t : T.left, ∃ U : X.left.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ ∀ z : Z.left, j.left z = t → i.left z ∈ U) (hPushout : IsPushout i.left j.left a.left b.left) : ∀ (H : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : yoneda.obj X ⟶ H.obj.obj) (g : yoneda.obj T ⟶ H.obj.obj), yoneda.map i ≫ f = yoneda.map j ≫ g → ∃! h : yoneda.obj P ⟶ H.obj.obj, yoneda.map a ≫ h = f ∧ yoneda.map b ≫ h = g

reviewed_lean.note: Statement matches Stacks 0EDP and the Situation at more-morphisms l.19708 clause by clause. i closed immersion, j integral with no finiteness, hAffine equals condition (3). IsPushout is the pushout in Scheme; asking for P, a, b over S adds nothing since a scheme pushout's map to S is unique. Maps into H are Yoneda on Over S, the same convention as AlgebraicSpace.lean (H.obj.obj : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u); there is no other scheme-to-space embedding. Conclusion ∃! h with ha=f and hb=g. Edge cases covered: Z empty, i or j identity, empty fibres, non-Noetherian, nonseparated H, any universe u. No duplicate found. lean.statement is verbatim in the file, longest line 92. Proof only sorry; docstrings carry source, blueprint id and all 4 steps. Plain import of the proof dep FerrandSchemePushout follows brief §3 rule 7. No change made, so no compile run. No findings.
